claims.statement: This reference applies to all three platforms and advises avoiding structured secret values for reliable matching/redaction.
Secret names allow alphanumerics/underscores, cannot start with a number or GITHUB_, are case-insensitive and stored uppercase, and must be unique in their creation scope.
More specific secret scopes override same-named broader values; repository overrides organization and environment has highest precedence.
Storage limits are1000 organization,100 repository and100 environment secrets; inventory limits are not a permission grant.
A workflow can access100 repository,100 organization and100 environment secrets; when assigned more than100 organization secrets only the alphabetically first100 are available.
Individual secrets are limited to48KB; larger-secret handling is a separate workaround with disclosure caveats.
Organization/repository secrets are read when a run is queued; environment secrets are read when their referencing job starts, so rotation timing is scope-dependent.

The reference lists automatic redaction patterns for32/64-byte Azure keys; Azure AD client application passwords; Azure Cache keys; Azure Container Registry keys; Azure Function host keys; Azure Search keys; database connection strings; HTTP Bearer headers; JWTs; npm author tokens; NuGet API keys; v1 GitHub installation tokens; v2 GitHub installation tokens listed as ghp, gho, ghu, ghs and ghr; and v2 PATs. This list does not guarantee redaction of arbitrary transformed values.
Unsupported redaction types may be proposed in the community discussion; this does not prove current detection of a missing pattern.
The secure-use reference is additional security guidance, not an executed audit.
